questions.explain: Statutory compliance covers the BR Act, RBI Act, RRB Act, FEMA and PMLA. Regulatory compliance covers guidelines of RBI, NABARD, SEBI and IRDAI.

questions.q: Following SEBI and IRDAI guidelines falls under which type of compliance?
questions.explain: Regulatory compliance means observing 'other regulatory guidelines issued from time to time by the regulators such as RBI, NABARD, SEBI, IRDAI, etc.'

questions.q: Complying with codes of BCSBI, IBA and FEDAI falls under which type of compliance?
questions.explain: Standards and codes of Income Tax, BCSBI, Ombudsman, IBA, FEDAI and the bank's internal policies 'are termed as other Compliances'.

questions.q: Who approves the Compliance Policy?
questions.explain: 'The Compliance Policy shall be approved by the Board.'

questions.q: Whom must the bank inform of the Chief Compliance Officer's name and any change in it?
questions.explain: 'NABARD will be kept informed of the name of the Chief Compliance Officer as also any change thereof.'

questions.q: What is the minimum rank of the Chief Compliance Officer (CCO)?
questions.explain: 'The CCO shall not be below the rank of a Senior Manager.'

questions.q: What is the minimum fixed tenure for which a CCO is appointed?
questions.explain: 'CCO shall be appointed for a minimum fixed tenure of not less than 3 years.'

questions.q: What is the maximum age for appointment as CCO?
questions.explain: 'Age: Not more than 55 years.'

questions.q: Who must approve the removal or transfer of the CCO?
questions.explain: 'CCO shall not be removed / transferred without the specific approval of the Board.'

questions.q: Which statement about the CCO's role is correct?
options: The CCO has no reporting relationship with business verticals and is given no business targets
The CCO is given deposit targets
The CCO is also the head of internal audit
The CCO reports to the head of credit
questions.explain: 'The CCO shall not have any reporting relationship with the business verticals of the Bank and shall not be given any business targets.'

questions.q: How often must the CCO assess compliance risk at a minimum?
questions.explain: The CCO must 'Conduct assessment of the Compliance Risk (at least once a year) and develop a risk-oriented activity plan', submitted to the ACB.

questions.q: How often must the HO Compliance Department report to the ACB and the Board?
options: Quarterly, plus an annual review to the ACB
questions.explain: 'The Compliance Department should submit quarterly report to the ACB & Board and Annual Review to ACB.'

questions.q: Who may compliance-test specialised areas like Forex, Investment and IT where the Compliance Department lacks expertise?
options: Officials deputed by the Sponsor Bank, at the CCO's request
questions.explain: For specialised areas, 'the Chief Compliance Officer may request Sponsor Bank to depute official(s) having requisite skills'.

questions.q: Who is the compliance officer of each functional department at Head Office?
questions.explain: 'HODs of functional departments at Head Office will be nominated as Compliance officer of their functional department.'

questions.q: Which committee is the CCO included in, to make sure new business products follow compliance rules?
questions.explain: 'In order to ensure adherence to compliance rules in new business product, CCO will be included in the New Product Development Committee (NPDC).'

questions.q: How often does the CCO meet the compliance officers (HODs) of Head Office departments?
questions.explain: 'CCO shall convene a quarterly meeting with the compliance officers (HODs) of functional departments at Head Office.'

questions.q: Who is the compliance officer at a Regional Office?
questions.explain: 'In Regional Offices, Regional Manager (RM) is the Compliance Officer.'

questions.q: To whom does the Regional Compliance Officer (RCO) report directly?
questions.explain: The RCO is under the RM's administrative control but should 'directly report to CCO/HO: Compliance Department'.

questions.q: What is the minimum rank of a Regional Compliance Officer?
questions.explain: 'The RCO shall not be below the rank of Manager.'

questions.q: What is the quorum for a Regional Level Compliance Committee (RLCC) meeting?
questions.explain: For RLCC meetings, 'Quorum is 4'.

questions.q: Who is the compliance officer at a branch?
questions.explain: 'At branches, the BMs will be performing the role of Compliance Officer.'

questions.q: Within how many days of the quarter's close must the Branch Manager send the Quarterly Compliance Certificate to the Regional Office?
questions.explain: The branch compliance officer must submit the certificate 'within 3 days from the close of the quarter'.

questions.q: Within what time must a branch report a breach or non-compliance to its Regional Office?
options: Two working days of observing it
At the end of the quarter
questions.explain: Branches must 'report any breaches / non-compliances observed within two working days of observing the breach'.

questions.q: Who reviews the compliance function's activities every year?
questions.explain: 'The activities of the compliance function should be subject to Annual Review by the Internal Audit.'

questions.q: Within how many working days must a branch acknowledge an LEA/IA request, stating whether the information is available and the turnaround time?
questions.explain: 'The branch should send an acknowledgement regarding availability of information/documents and turnaround time (TAT) ... within three (03) working days.'

questions.q: If an LEA asks before 4 PM for a debit freeze on a suspicious account, when must the action be acknowledged to the agency?
options: At the end of the month
questions.explain: 'The acknowledgment regarding debit freeze/stop/hold & action taken thereof must be intimated to the agency the same day (if request is made by LEA before 4 PM).'

questions.q: When cyber police give urgent freeze instructions by phone, SMS or WhatsApp, within what time must a written letter or email follow?
questions.explain: 'These verbal instructions should be followed by authorized letter/email of the appropriate authority within one (1) working day.'

questions.q: For matters not covered by the SOP, what is the maximum time to give details to the agencies?
questions.explain: 'For anything not written in the SOP, the maximum time-limit would be six (6) weeks to furnish the details.'

questions.q: The PSL guidelines covered in the material are based on which RBI Master Direction?
questions.explain: The cover slide cites 'RBI Master Directions BC. RBI/FIDD/2024-25/128 Dated March 24, 2025'.

questions.q: From what date are the revised PSL guidelines effective?
questions.explain: 'RBI has revised the existing Priority Sector Lending guidelines w.e.f. 01/04/2025.'

questions.q: In which year was the description of the priority sector formalised?
questions.explain: 'National Credit Council held in 1968. Description of Priority Sector formalized in 1972.'

questions.q: In 1974, what share of total advances was decided for priority sector advances by March 1979?
questions.explain: 'In 1974 it was decided that share of PSAs should increase to 33 1/3% of total advances by March 1979.'

questions.q: What is the overall PSL target for Regional Rural Banks?
options: 40% of ANBC or CEOBE, whichever is higher
75% of ANBC or CEOBE, whichever is higher
questions.explain: RRBs: '75% of ANBC or CEOBE whichever is higher.'

questions.q: For RRBs, lending to which segments counts towards PSL achievement only up to 15% of ANBC?
options: Medium Enterprises, Social Infrastructure and Renewable Energy
questions.explain: For RRBs, 'lending to Medium Enterprises, Social Infrastructure and Renewable Energy shall be reckoned for priority sector achievement only up to 15% of ANBC'.

questions.q: What is the overall PSL target for Small Finance Banks?
options: 60% of ANBC or CEOBE, whichever is higher
questions.explain: Small Finance Banks: '60 per cent of ANBC ... or CEOBE whichever is higher.'

questions.q: What does CEOBE stand for?
options: Central Exposure on Bonds and Equity
Cumulative Export Obligation of Banking Entities
Credit Equivalent amount of Off-Balance Sheet Exposure
questions.explain: 'CEOBE: Credit Equivalent of Off Balance Sheet Exposure', as defined in the targets summary.

questions.q: What is the agriculture target for domestic commercial banks, RRBs and SFBs?
options: 18% of ANBC or CEOBE, whichever is higher
questions.explain: The agriculture target is '18 per cent ANBC or CEOBE, whichever is higher'.

questions.q: Within the 18% agriculture target, what sub-target is set for Non-Corporate Farmers?
questions.explain: 'Within this target, 14 percent is prescribed for Non Corporate Farmers, out of which a target of 10 percent is prescribed for SMFs.'

questions.q: What sub-target is set for Small and Marginal Farmers (SMFs)?
questions.explain: Out of the 14% for Non-Corporate Farmers, 'a target of 10 percent is prescribed for SMFs'.

questions.q: What is the sub-target for Micro Enterprises?
options: 7.5% of ANBC or CEOBE, whichever is higher
questions.explain: 'Micro Enterprises: 7.5 percent of ANBC or Credit Equivalent Amount of Off-Balance Sheet Exposure, whichever is higher.'

questions.q: What is the Weaker Sections target for RRBs?
options: 15% of ANBC or CEOBE, whichever is higher
questions.explain: 'Weaker Section: 12% target ... for Domestic Commercial Banks, SFBs & Foreign Banks with 20 branches and above and 15% for RRB.'

questions.q: From FY 2024-25, what weight is given to incremental PSL credit in districts where per capita PSL is below Rs. 9,000?
questions.explain: 'A higher weight (125%) would be assigned to the incremental priority sector credit in the identified districts where ... per capita PSL less than Rs. 9,000.'

questions.q: Are RRBs subject to the district-level adjustment of weights in PSL achievement?
questions.explain: 'Regional Rural Banks are exempted from adjustments of weights in PSL achievement due to their currently limited area of operation.'

questions.q: Up to what amount do loans to individual farmers against pledge of produce, backed by NWRs/eNWRs for up to 12 months, qualify as farm credit?
questions.explain: 'Loans up to Rs. 90 lakh against pledge/hypothecation of agricultural produce ... against NWRs/eNWRs and up to Rs. 60 lakh against warehouse receipts other than NWRs/eNWRs.'

questions.q: What is the landholding limit for a 'Marginal Farmer'?
options: More than 1 and up to 2 hectares
questions.explain: 'Marginal Farmer: Farmer Landholding up to 1 hectare; Small Farmer: more than 1 hectare and up to 2 hectare.'

questions.q: Up to what aggregate sanction limit per borrower from the banking system do agriculture infrastructure loans qualify?
questions.explain: Agriculture infrastructure covers 'Loan for aggregate sanction limit of Rs. 100 crore per borrower from the banking system'.

questions.q: Under the revised MSME classification, what are the limits for a Micro Enterprise?
options: Investment below Rs. 10 crore and turnover below Rs. 50 crore
Investment below Rs. 25 crore and turnover below Rs. 100 crore
Investment below Rs. 2.5 crore and turnover below Rs. 10 crore
Investment below Rs. 1 crore and turnover below Rs. 5 crore
questions.explain: 'Micro Enterprises: Investment < 2.5 Cr & Turnover < 10 Cr.' Small: < 25 Cr & < 100 Cr. Medium: < 125 Cr & < 500 Cr.

questions.q: Under the revised MSME classification, what are the limits for a Medium Enterprise?
options: Investment below Rs. 25 crore and turnover below Rs. 100 crore
Investment below Rs. 50 crore and turnover below Rs. 250 crore
Investment below Rs. 100 crore and turnover below Rs. 1,000 crore
Investment below Rs. 125 crore and turnover below Rs. 500 crore
questions.explain: 'Medium Enterprises: Investment < 125 Cr & Turnover < 500 Cr.'

questions.q: What is the maximum overdraft limit for PMJDY account holders that counts towards PSL?
questions.explain: 'Maximum overdraft limit to Pradhan Mantri Jan-Dhan Yojana (PMJDY) account holders stands at Rs. 10,000/-.'

questions.q: Up to what amount do loans to start-ups qualify under PSL?
questions.explain: 'Loans up to Rs. 50 crore to Start-ups, as per definition of Ministry of Commerce and Industry, Govt. of India.'

questions.q: Up to what amount do education loans to individuals (including vocational courses) qualify for PSL?
questions.explain: 'Loans to individuals for educational purposes, including vocational courses, not exceeding Rs. 25 lakh will be considered as eligible for priority sector classification.'

questions.q: Up to what limit do bank loans for building healthcare facilities (including under Ayushman Bharat) in Tier II to Tier VI centres qualify as social infrastructure?
questions.explain: Social infrastructure: up to Rs. 8 crore for schools, drinking water and sanitation, and 'up to a limit of Rs. 12 crore per borrower for building health care facilities'.

questions.q: What is the renewable energy loan limit per borrower for individual households?
questions.explain: Renewable energy loans qualify up to Rs. 35 crore for borrowers, and 'For individual households, the loan limit will be Rs. 10 lakh per borrower'.

questions.q: For housing loans in centres with population of 50 lakh and above, what are the loan limit and maximum cost of the dwelling unit?
options: Loan up to Rs. 35 lakh; dwelling cost up to Rs. 44 lakh
Loan up to Rs. 45 lakh; dwelling cost up to Rs. 57 lakh
Loan up to Rs. 50 lakh; dwelling cost up to Rs. 63 lakh
Loan up to Rs. 15 lakh; dwelling cost up to Rs. 50 lakh
questions.explain: For centres with population of 50 lakh and above: loan limit Rs. 50 lakh (purchase/construction), Rs. 15 lakh (repairs), maximum dwelling cost Rs. 63 lakh.

questions.q: Which housing loans are excluded from priority sector?
options: Loans for repair of damaged dwellings
Loans to government agencies for slum clearance
Housing loans to the bank's own employees
Loans to individuals in centres below 10 lakh population
questions.explain: 'The housing loans to banks' own employees will be excluded.'

questions.q: Through which platform are Priority Sector Lending Certificates (PSLCs) traded?
questions.explain: 'The PSLCs will be traded through the CBS portal (e-Kuber) of RBI.'

questions.q: What is the standard lot size of PSLCs, and when do they expire?
options: Rs. 10 lakh; they expire after one year from sale
Rs. 1 crore; they expire on 30 September
Rs. 25 lakh and multiples; they expire on 31 March
questions.explain: 'All PSLCs will expire by March 31st ... The PSLCs would have a standard lot size of Rs. 25 lakh and multiples thereof.'

questions.q: RRBs may issue Inter Bank Participation Certificates (IBPCs) to scheduled commercial banks for priority sector advances in excess of what share of their outstanding advances?
questions.explain: 'RRBs are allowed to issue IBPCs to Scheduled Commercial Banks in respect of their priority sector advances in excess of 75 percent of their outstanding advances.'

questions.q: Which section of the Banking Regulation Act, 1949 defines 'banking'?
questions.explain: The definition of banking is from 'Sec 5(b) of the Banking Regulation Act, 1949'.

questions.q: Who gave the definition of 'customer' known as the 'Duration Theory'?
questions.explain: 'According to John Paget, a Customer constitutes a person who has an account with a bank ... popularly known as the Duration Theory.'

questions.q: Under which Act must a bank make sure the customer is legally capable of entering into a valid contract?
questions.explain: Banking is a contract, so the customer must be 'legally capable of entering into a valid contract' under the Indian Contract Act, 1872.

questions.q: Does the RBI require an introduction by an existing customer to open an account?
options: No; banks should not insist on an introduction
questions.explain: 'RBI has informed that introduction is not necessary for opening of accounts.'

questions.q: In a joint account with the instruction 'Former or Survivor', who can change or revoke the operating instructions?
questions.explain: 'In joint accounts with operational instructions Former or Survivor, instructions can be changed/revoked only by Former.'

questions.q: In an 'Either or Survivor' joint account, who can request premature payment of an FDR?
questions.explain: The joint account summary lists premature payment of an FDR as 'Any one' for Either or Survivor, 'Only Former' for Former or Survivor, and 'All jointly' for Joint operation.

questions.q: In any type of joint account, who must give a stop payment instruction?
questions.explain: The joint account summary lists 'Stop Payment – All jointly' for all three types of joint account.

questions.q: Under Section 3 of the Indian Majority Act, at what age does a person whose guardian is appointed by a court attain majority?
questions.explain: 'A person attains majority at the age of 18, except in cases where a guardian is appointed by a Court where the age of majority is 21.'

questions.q: Which Act recognises either parent (father or mother) as natural guardian?
options: Section 6(a) of the Hindu Minority and Guardianship Act, 1956
Section 3 of the Indian Majority Act
questions.explain: 'Section 6(a) of Hindu Minority and Guardianship Act, 1956 recognizes that either of the parents, father or mother, can be the natural guardian.'

questions.q: From what age may literate minors open and operate savings bank accounts on their own?
questions.explain: 'Literate Minors above the age of 10 years may be now allowed to open and operate savings bank accounts independently.'

questions.q: Which account should NOT be opened for a minor?
questions.explain: For minor accounts: 'No Current Account should be opened. No loan is given to minor.'

questions.q: A guardian appointed by a will is called:
questions.explain: Types of guardian: Natural Guardian, Testamentary Guardian (appointed by will), Legal Guardian (appointed by court).

questions.q: Under Mohammedan law, who is the natural guardian of a Muslim minor?
questions.explain: 'Account of mohammedan minors are to be operated upon by father who is the natural guardian & mother can not act as natural guardian under Mohammedan Law.'

questions.q: If the guardian dies while the minor is alive, how is the minor's account treated?
options: It is closed and paid to the guardian's legal heirs
As a trust, payable to the minor on attaining majority
It is transferred to the bank's unclaimed deposits
questions.explain: 'When the guardian dies (but minor is alive) the account is treated as a trust and is to be paid to the minor when he attains majority.'

questions.q: For an illiterate person, which thumb impressions are normally taken?
options: Right hand thumb for males, left hand thumb for females
Left hand thumb for males, right hand thumb for females
questions.explain: 'Normally, Left Hand Thumb impression (LHT) of male & Right Hand Thumb impression (RHT) of female is to be obtained.'

questions.q: How many identification marks should be taken from an illiterate customer on the account opening form?
questions.explain: 'In the account opening form the banker should obtain two identification marks from the illiterate person.'

questions.q: Which statement about blind customers is correct?
options: All banking facilities, including net banking, ATM, cheque book, locker and loans, must be offered without discrimination
They can open only fixed deposits
questions.explain: 'All banking facilities including net banking, ATM, Cheque Book, Locker facility, loans to be offered to visually challenged customers without discrimination.'

questions.q: Who attests the signature of a married pardanashin woman?
questions.explain: 'Her signature to be attested by her husband in case of married woman & by natural guardian in case of unmarried girl.'

questions.q: Under Hindu law, which communities can form an HUF?
questions.explain: 'As per Hindu law, the Hindus, Sikhs & Jains can form HUF.'

questions.q: Which school of Hindu law governs HUFs in Bengal?
questions.explain: 'In Bengal, it is governed by Dayabhag law; in other parts of India, it is governed by Mitakshara Law.'

questions.q: Who manages HUF property?
options: The Karta, the senior-most major male member
questions.explain: 'HUF property is managed by senior most major male member called Manager or Karta.'

questions.q: Which letter must the Karta and all coparceners sign for an HUF account?
questions.explain: 'Joint Hindu Family Letter (CD-115) to be signed by Karta & all the coparceners.'

questions.q: Can an HUF enter into a partnership?
options: No, per a 1998 Supreme Court judgement
questions.explain: 'HUF cannot enter into a partnership as per Supreme Court judgement of 1998.'

questions.q: Under the Companies Act, 2013, what is the maximum number of partners in a firm (excluding minors)?
questions.explain: 'As per Companies Act 2013, Maximum number of partner can be up to 100 (excluding minor) in a firm.'

questions.q: In a partnership firm account, which partner can stop a cheque issued by another partner?
options: Only the partner who issued it
questions.explain: 'Any partner can stop cheque issued by another partner.'

questions.q: Which Act governs Limited Liability Partnerships?
questions.explain: 'LLP is governed by limited liability partnership Act 2008.' It needs a minimum of 2 designated partners.

questions.q: What are the minimum and maximum numbers of members in a private limited company?
questions.explain: 'Private Limited Company – Members: Min. 2 members, Max. 200 members.'

questions.q: What minimum share of paid-up capital must the Government hold for a company to be a Government company?
questions.explain: 'Government company means any company in which not less than fifty one percent of the paid-up share capital is held by the Central Government, or by any State Government.'

questions.q: Which document is called the 'document of indoor management' of a company?
questions.explain: 'Article of Association – (Also known as Document of Indoor Management) Regulations controlling internal management of the company.'

questions.q: Which Act governs trusts?
questions.explain: 'Trusts are governed by the Indian Trust Act, 1882.' If the trust deed is silent on operations, all trustees operate the account jointly.

quizzes.topic: Legal Policies – Compensation, Document Retention and Death Claims

questions.q: Who is the custodian of the Document Handling and Retention Policy?
questions.explain: 'The General Manager will be the custodian of the Policy. Department in charge of Legal will implement, maintain and periodically update the policy.'

questions.q: Which files must be kept permanently?
options: Confidential files, and files on industrial disputes, writ petitions, CBI, fraud and court cases
questions.explain: 'Confidential Files and Files relating to Industrial Disputes and Writ Petitions/Files pertaining to CBI/Fraud/Court Cases ... are to be preserved permanently.'

questions.q: Why can't records of unclaimed deposits be destroyed?
options: Because the liability remains outstanding until the amount is paid
Because they are needed for tax returns
questions.explain: 'In case of unclaimed deposits, the liability continues to be outstanding and the banks are required to maintain / preserve the records.'

questions.q: For written-off loans whose credit guarantee claims are settled, how long are papers kept after closure?
options: 5 years, provided there is no chance of recovery
questions.explain: Such loan papers 'be maintained for a period of 5 years from the date of closure and later eliminated, provided there is no chance of recovery'.

questions.q: By what date each year must the list of records proposed for destruction be sent to Head Office for approval?
questions.explain: The list of records to be destroyed 'shall be submitted to the Head Office for seeking approval on or before 31st August every year'.

questions.q: Where are the proceeds from selling destroyed records credited?
questions.explain: 'The proceeds should be credited to Miscellaneous Income Account, giving full details as to weight of the records, rate etc.'

questions.q: From what date did the PML (Maintenance of Records) Rules, 2005 come into force?
questions.explain: The PML Rules, 2005 'has come into force from 1st July 2005'.

questions.q: Under the PML rules, how long must customer identification and address records be kept after the business relationship ends?
questions.explain: Identification records must be 'properly preserved for at least five years after the business relationship is ended'.

questions.q: Under the revised Tamil Nadu stamp duty (Legal Dept Cir 47/2024-25), what stamp duty applies to an Indemnity Bond?
questions.explain: The revised stamp duties: Agreement – Rs. 200; Affidavit – Rs. 200; Indemnity Bond – Rs. 500; General Power of Attorney – Rs. 1,000; Special Power of Attorney – Rs. 500.

questions.q: What stamp duty applies to a General Power of Attorney (other than one for selling property)?
questions.explain: 'General Power of Attorney other than for selling a property – Rs. 1000/-.'

questions.q: What happens to the court fee if a case is referred to Lok Adalat and settled there?
options: The court fee originally paid in the civil court is refunded
The court fee goes to the bank
questions.explain: 'If a matter is referred for settlement in Lok Adalat and is settled subsequently, court fee originally paid in the civil court by the petitioner will also be refunded back to the party.'

questions.q: For an unauthorised or erroneous debit where verification involves a third party, within what time must the process be completed?
questions.explain: 'If the verification involves third party – within one month complete the process. If the verification does not involve third party – within 7 days.'

questions.q: If a cheque is paid after a stop-payment instruction, within what time must the bank reverse it?
questions.explain: 'Payment of Cheques after Stop Payment Instructions shall be reversed within 2 working days', with any consequential loss compensated within 2 working days.

questions.q: What is the clearing norm for local cheques?
questions.explain: 'Local clearing cheques – clearing norms ranging from 48 to 72 hours', with savings bank interest paid for delays.

questions.q: What is the maximum collection period for outstation cheques drawn on state capitals?
questions.explain: Outstation cheques: State Capitals – 7 days; Major cities – 10 days; All other centres – 14 days.

questions.q: What interest is paid for extraordinary delays (over 90 days) in collecting outstation cheques?
questions.explain: 'In case of extraordinary delay (i.e., delays exceeding 90 days) – Term deposit + 2%.'

questions.q: What compensation applies to delays in crediting NEFT/RTGS/NECS/ECS proceeds beyond one day due to the bank's fault?
questions.explain: The compensation 'shall be the current Repo Rate plus Two percent', credited even if no claim is lodged.

questions.q: What is the maximum compensation for failure to execute a standing instruction?
questions.explain: The bank compensates 'to the extent of the financial loss not exceeding Rs. 100/- per occasion'; GM approval is needed.

questions.q: Within what time must a duplicate demand draft be issued?
options: A fortnight from receiving the request
questions.explain: 'Duplicate Draft will be issued within a fortnight from the receipt of such request', with FD interest for delays beyond that.

questions.q: A customer reports an unauthorised electronic transaction within 3 working days of receiving the bank's communication. What is the customer's liability?
questions.explain: 'Within 3 working days – Zero liability.'

questions.q: What is the customer's maximum liability for an unauthorised transaction in a BSBD account (reported in 4–7 working days)?
questions.explain: The maximum liability table lists BSBD accounts at Rs. 5,000.

questions.q: Within how many days of full repayment must the bank return securities and title deeds to borrowers, per the lender's liability commitments?
questions.explain: The bank 'would return to our borrowers all the securities / documents / title deeds ... within 15 days of repayment of all dues'.

questions.q: If an ATM failure is not re-credited within 7 working days of the complaint, what compensation is paid?
questions.explain: 'Bank shall pay compensation of Rs. 100/- per day to the aggrieved customer.'

questions.q: Who is authorised to approve compensation of up to Rs. 10,000?
questions.explain: Authority to pay compensation: Up to Rs. 10,000 – GM; Rs. 10,001 to Rs. 1,00,000 – Chairman; above Rs. 1 lakh – Board.

questions.q: If the bank delays releasing property documents beyond 30 days after full repayment, what compensation is payable?
options: Rs. 5,000 for each day of delay
questions.explain: Where the delay is attributable to the RE, 'it shall compensate the borrower at the rate of Rs. 5,000/- for each day of delay'.

questions.q: In a joint deposit account, when does the nominee's right arise?
options: On the death of the first depositor
Only after the death of all the depositors
On the death of any one depositor
questions.explain: 'In the case of a joint deposit account with or without survivorship clause, the nominee's right arises only after the death of all the depositors.'

questions.q: What is the threshold limit for settling death claims without a nominee or survivorship clause, without a surety bond?
questions.explain: 'Threshold limit means Claims up to Rs. 20.00 Lakhs.' No third-party surety bond is needed up to this limit.

questions.q: Within what time must the bank settle a deceased customer's deposit claim after receiving all documents?
questions.explain: 'Bank should settle a claim ... within a period not exceeding 15 calendar days from the date of receipt of all the required documents.'

questions.q: If a deposit death claim is delayed due to the bank, at what rate is compensation paid?
options: Not less than the prevailing Bank Rate + 4% per annum
questions.explain: Compensation is 'in the form of interest, at a rate not less than the prevailing Bank Rate + 4 percent per annum'. For lockers, it is Rs. 5,000 per day.

questions.q: For a missing person's account where the amount payable is less than Rs. 1 lakh, what can be accepted instead of a death certificate or court order?
options: A copy of the FIR and the police's non-traceable report
A letter from the village officer
questions.explain: 'Where the aggregate amount payable ... is less than Rs. 1 lakh, a copy of the First Information Report (FIR) and non-traceable report issued by police authorities shall be obtained.'

quizzes.topic: FI Policies – Financial Inclusion and Financial Literacy Centres

questions.q: When did the RBI release the National Strategy for Financial Inclusion (NSFI) 2019-2024?
questions.explain: 'On January 10, 2020, RBI released National Strategy for Financial Inclusion for India (NSFI) 2019-2024.'

questions.q: In which year did the RBI introduce the Business Correspondent (BC) and Business Facilitator (BF) model?
questions.explain: 'RBI in 2006 had introduced the BC & BF Model.'

questions.q: What is the difference between a Business Correspondent and a Business Facilitator?
options: BCs can transact on the bank's behalf as agents; BFs can refer clients but cannot transact
Both can transact on the bank's behalf
questions.explain: 'Business Correspondents (BCs) were permitted to carry out transaction on behalf of the Banks as agents. Business Facilitators (BFs) ... cannot transact on behalf of Banks.'

questions.q: Since when have banks been allowed to provide Aadhaar-based e-KYC services?
questions.explain: 'In September 2013, Banks were allowed to provide e-KYC services based on Aadhaar.'

questions.q: Under NSFI's 'Universal Access' pillar, every village should have a formal financial service provider within what radius?
questions.explain: 'Universal Access to Financial Services – Every village to have access to a formal financial service provider within a reasonable distance of 5 KM radius.'

questions.q: Under NSFI 2025-30 ('Panch-Jyoti'), what target share of women Business Correspondents is set for December 2028?
questions.explain: 'Gender-Sensitive Inclusion: Increasing women business correspondents (BCs) to a 30% target share by December 2028.'

questions.q: How many households should a BC deal with, per the guidelines?
questions.explain: 'BCs should be dealing with 1000-1500 households, or cater to a population of about 5000-8000.'

questions.q: What is the maximum distance between a BC and the base branch in rural, semi-urban and urban areas?
questions.explain: 'The distance between BC and the base branch should not exceed 30 KMs in rural, semi-urban and urban areas & 5 KMs in metropolitan centres.'

questions.q: Who is the bank's Grievance Redressal Officer for deficiencies in BC services?
questions.explain: 'General Manager (Credit) is the Grievance Redressal Officer (GRO) of our Bank and the Regional Managers are designated as GRO at Regional Level.'

questions.q: Which bodies jointly developed the Jan Dhan Darshak mobile app?
options: The Department of Financial Services (DFS) and the National Informatics Centre (NIC)
The Ministry of MSME and NIC
questions.explain: 'Department of Financial Services (DFS), Ministry of Finance and National Informatics Centre (NIC) has jointly developed a mobile app called Jan Dhan Darshak.'

questions.q: On what basis does the bank sign its model agreement with Corporate BCs?
questions.explain: 'Bank shall execute the model agreement on Principal to Principal basis to minimize the legal risks and liabilities.'

questions.q: What minimum existence does an entity need to be appointed as a Corporate BC / Service Provider?
options: At least 3 years, with a good track record
questions.explain: 'The entity shall have been in existence for at least 3 years with a good track record', with recoveries of not less than 70%.

questions.q: What Bank Guarantee does the bank take from Corporate BCs as collateral security?
questions.explain: 'Bank will obtain collateral security from the Corporate BCs in the form Bank Guarantee (BG) of Rs. 25,00,000/-.'

questions.q: What penalty applies if a BC agent does not function for more than 10 working days in a row?
options: Rs. 500 per day, with no maximum
Rs. 1,000 per day from the 11th day, up to Rs. 10,000 per month per centre
questions.explain: 'A penalty @ Rs. 1000/- per day (from the 11th day onwards) ... with a maximum of Rs. 10,000/- per month per centre.'

questions.q: What is the age range for a BC Agent?
questions.explain: 'The age of the proposed BC Agent should be between 18 to 60 Years.' The minimum qualification is a 10th Standard pass.

questions.q: What is the BC overdraft (OD) limit?
options: Rs. 50,000, brought to zero at least once a day
questions.explain: 'BC OD limit is fixed as Rs. 50,000/-. All BC Agents must bring their OD account to Zero at least once in a day.' RMs may allow up to Rs. 1,00,000 for up to 7 days.

questions.q: Within what radius of the base village's geo-location can BC agents perform AEPS transactions?
questions.explain: 'BCAs will only be able to perform AEPS transactions within 20 km radius from the geo-location of the BCA's base village.'

questions.q: Which of these services is NOT available at a BC point?
questions.explain: Services not available at BC points include accounts of 0–10 year olds, lunatics' and foreign nationals' accounts, blind persons' accounts, adding/deleting joint holders, and freezing and closing accounts.

questions.q: Under the extended PMJDY, what is the overdraft limit and the age limit?
questions.explain: 'Existing Overdraft limit ... of Rs. 5000/- has been raised to Rs. 10,000/-. Age Limit of 18-60 years has been raised to 18-65 years.'

questions.q: If a BC agent is continuously absent without valid reason, after how long are they treated as inactive?
questions.explain: 'If BC agent is continuously absent for more than thirty days without valid reasons will be considered as inactive.'

questions.q: How often must rural branches hold a financial literacy camp?
options: At least one camp a month, on the third Friday after branch hours
questions.explain: 'Rural branches of banks are required to conduct at least one camp per month (Third Friday of each month after branch hours).'

questions.q: What are the working hours of a Financial Literacy Centre?
options: 5 days a week, 10.00 AM to 4.00 PM
6 days a week, 9.00 AM to 5.00 PM
7 days a week, 10.00 AM to 2.00 PM
questions.explain: 'Working time 5 days a week between 10.00 AM to 4.00 PM.'

questions.q: What minimum service does an FLC counsellor need?
options: 20 years, including at least 5 years in the officer cadre
questions.explain: 'Candidate should have retired ... with minimum 20 years of service of which at least 5 years in Officer Cadre.'

questions.q: What monthly remuneration is paid to a newly engaged FLC counsellor?
questions.explain: 'A consolidated amount of Rs. 14,000/- per month will be paid ... After completion of 2 years, revised remuneration of Rs. 16,000/-.'

questions.q: When was PMJDY launched?
questions.explain: 'The scheme is launched by Govt. of India in 28th August 2014 (announced on the independence day speech on 15th August 2014).'

questions.q: What life cover does PMJJBY give for death due to any reason?
questions.explain: 'PMJJBY is an Insurance scheme that offers Rs. 2 Lakh life insurance cover for death due to any reason.'

questions.q: What is the lien period under PMJJBY, during which cover is not available (except for accidental death)?
questions.explain: 'Insurance Cover will not be available for the first 30 days (Lien Period) from date of enrolment, however the same is not applicable for death due to accident.'

questions.q: What is the entry age for PMSBY?
questions.explain: 'The entry age of the customer should be between 18 to 70 years. The exit age of the scheme will be 70 years.'

questions.q: What is the annual premium per member under PMSBY?
questions.explain: 'Insurance Premium is Rs. 20 per year per member.'

questions.q: What is the entry age for the Atal Pension Yojana (APY)?
questions.explain: 'The entry age of the customer should be between 18 to 40 years.' The subscriber gets a pension of Rs. 1,000–5,000 after age 60.

quizzes.topic: Customer Grievance Redressal, Bancassurance, Lockers, Customer Service and Deposits

questions.q: If a customer's complaint is not resolved within what period can they approach the Banking Ombudsman?
questions.explain: 'If a customer's complaint is not resolved within a period of one month or if he/she is not satisfied with the solution provided by the bank, he/she can approach the Banking Ombudsman.'

questions.q: How often does the Standing Committee on Customer Service meet?
questions.explain: The Standing Committee on Customer Service 'would meet once in a quarter' to review service quality and unresolved complaints.

questions.q: Who is the bank's Nodal Officer for customer service and complaint handling?
options: The General Manager in charge of Customer Service
questions.explain: 'General Manager in-charge of Customer Service would be the Nodal Officer responsible for implementation of Customer Service and complaint handling mechanism.'

questions.q: Who acts as Customer Relation Officer in each region?
options: The Nodal Officer at Head Office
questions.explain: 'ALL RM – CUSTOMER RELATION OFFICER IN THEIR RESPECTIVE REGION.'

questions.q: Under SPGRS, within how many days must the branch resolve a complaint before it escalates?
questions.explain: 'Branch would resolve within 5 days from the date of receipt of the complaint, if not by Regional Office within 10 days ... and Head Office totally within 21 days.'

questions.q: What is the maximum time to resolve a complaint under SPGRS?
questions.explain: Complaints are resolved 'within the given time frame viz. 21 days'.

questions.q: When can customers meet the Branch Manager to resolve grievances?
options: At 3.00 pm on the 15th of every month (or the next working day)
On the last Friday of every month
On any working day after 4.00 pm
questions.explain: 'Customers can meet the Branch Manager at 3.00 pm on 15th of every month or on the next working day, if it falls on Saturday or on a holiday.'

questions.q: What action is taken on anonymous complaints?
options: No action; they are simply filed
They are forwarded to the RBI
They are answered in a newspaper
questions.explain: 'No action is required to be taken on anonymous complaints, irrespective of the nature of allegations and such complaints need to be simply filed.'

questions.q: Under which IRDAI licence number is the bank a Corporate Agent?
questions.explain: 'Our Bank is Corporate Agent for Life Insurance, General Insurance and Health Insurance business, under license No. CA0072 issued by IRDAI.'

questions.q: What is the maximum total number of insurer arrangements (life, general and health) a Corporate Agent can have at any time?
questions.explain: Up to nine insurers per segment are allowed, and 'The total number of arrangements with life, general and health insurers, shall not exceed twenty-seven at any point of time.'

questions.q: What is the bancassurance business mix in the policy?
questions.explain: 'Business Mix: Life Insurance – 50%, General Insurance – 45%, Health Insurance – 5%.'

questions.q: Within how many days must the bank redress insurance-related client grievances?
questions.explain: 'The bank shall take adequate steps for redressal of grievances of the clients within 14 days of receipt of such complaint.'

questions.q: In the bancassurance escalation matrix, who is the final point of grievance redressal?
questions.explain: 'Final Level: If for any reason the complaint is not resolved, the Principal Officer of the Bank shall be the final point of grievance redressal.'

questions.q: What is the penalty under Section 102 of the IRDA Act, 1999 for default?
questions.explain: 'Sec 102 of IRDA ACT, 1999, penalty for default in complying with is Rs 1 crore' (revised from Rs. 5 lakh).

questions.q: What is the legal relationship between the bank and a locker hirer?
questions.explain: 'The relationship between the banker and the locker hirer(s) is that of a lessor and lessee.'

questions.q: For how long must CCTV recordings of the strong room's entry and exit be kept?
questions.explain: The CCTV recording 'should be preserved for a period of not less than 180 days'.

questions.q: How many nominees are allowed for an individual locker account?
questions.explain: 'In case of Individual Locker Account, only one Nominee is permitted and under Joint Locker Account, one or more Nominees are permitted.'

questions.q: If lockers must be moved due to a branch merger, closure or shift, how much advance notice must customers get?
questions.explain: The bank shall give public notice in two newspapers and 'the customers shall be intimated at least two months in advance'.

questions.q: For which period is annual locker rent recovered?
questions.explain: 'Currently annual locker rent is being recovered for the period from July to June', plus 18% GST.

questions.q: What penalty applies if locker rent is unpaid in the second quarter after the due date?
questions.explain: Penalty: I Quarter – 10% of the rent; II Quarter – 20%; III Quarter – 25%.

questions.q: After how long of non-payment of locker rent is break-open action started?
questions.explain: 'The process for breaking open to be initiated, if the locker rent has not been paid by the hirer(s) for three years in a row.'

questions.q: When can a locker be broken open even if the rent is paid regularly?
options: When it has not been operated for more than seven years
When the key is in the bank's custody
questions.explain: 'In case the locker remains inoperable for more than seven years, the branch shall have the right to cancel the allotment of the locker and break open the locker, even if the rent is paid regularly.'

questions.q: In whose presence must a locker be broken open?
options: A bank officer and two independent witnesses
questions.explain: 'The locker shall be broken open in the presence of an Officer of the Bank and two independent Witnesses', with video recording where possible.

questions.q: Who can NOT be accepted as an attorney to operate a locker?
options: An adult nominated by all joint hirers
A minor, or a bank employee
A person holding a stamped Power of Attorney
questions.explain: 'A minor should not be accepted as an attorney ... An Officer or other employee of the Bank should not be permitted to be an attorney.'

questions.q: What is the bank's liability for loss of locker contents from fire, theft, burglary, building collapse or employee fraud?
options: 100 times the prevailing annual locker rent
The full value of the contents
questions.explain: 'Bank's liability shall be for an amount equivalent to one hundred times the prevailing annual rent of the safe deposit locker.'

questions.q: If a change in terms is adverse to the customer, how much prior notice must be given?
questions.explain: 'If the change is adverse to the customer, prior notice of minimum 30 days will be provided.'

questions.q: Within how many working days must the bank acknowledge a formal complaint, per the Customer Service policy?
questions.explain: 'Acknowledge all formal complaints ... within three working days and work to resolve it within a reasonable period, not exceeding 30 days.'

questions.q: Above what amount is a single rupee term deposit a 'bulk deposit' for RRBs, per the policy text?
questions.explain: 'Bulk Deposit is defined as single rupee term deposit of Rupees fifteen lakhs and above' for RRBs. (Cir 113-2023-24 refers to bulk deposits of one crore and above.)

questions.q: What uniform interest rate now applies to savings balances (Cir 15/2026-27)?
questions.explain: 'Cir 15 2026-27 discontinuation of tiered rate of interest for sb account. Now uniform interest 3.25 for savings balance.'

questions.q: What additional interest over the card rate is paid to senior citizens on special deposit schemes?
questions.explain: 'Bank will pay additional interest presently 0.50% over card rate' to senior citizens; for deposits above Rs. 3 crore, only the card rate applies.

questions.q: The bank's outstanding unsecured advances (including unsecured guarantees) must not exceed what share of total outstanding advances?
questions.explain: 'Bank's outstanding unsecured advances (including unsecured guarantees) should not exceed 30% of its total outstanding advances.'

questions.q: What is the exposure limit for a single borrower, as a share of the bank's net worth?
questions.explain: Exposure limits: Single borrower – 15%; Single (Infrastructure) – 20%; Group – 40%; Group (Infrastructure) – 50% of net worth.

questions.q: What is the exposure limit for housing loans?
options: 5% of total advances as on March of the previous FY
questions.explain: The sector limits are: Loan to MFIs for on-lending – 2% of total advances; Housing Loan – 5% of total advances; Collateral Management Loan – Rs. 20 crores.

questions.q: When is an exposure 'unsecured'?
options: When the security value is below 50% of the exposure
When the loan is below Rs. 2 lakh
When the market value of the security is not more than 10% of the outstanding exposure
questions.explain: 'Unsecured exposure is defined as an exposure where the market value of security ... is not more than 10% of the outstanding exposure.'

questions.q: What is the entry-level CIBIL score for 'All Other loans'?
questions.explain: The entry-level scores are 550 (CIBIL) for gold collateral loans above the exempt limits, and 700 (CIBIL) for all other loans.

questions.q: How are MSME proposals with CIBIL MSME Rank (CMR) 7–10 treated?
options: They are not to be considered
questions.explain: 'Entry Level Score: 1-4 category. Proposals for CMR 5-6 category to be considered only with the availability of 100% collateral security. Proposal with CMR 7-10 is not to be considered.'

questions.q: How many digits does a Legal Entity Identifier (LEI) have?
questions.explain: The Legal Entity Identifier is a '20-digit number' for financial transactions.

questions.q: Above what credit exposure does the bank advise borrowers to obtain an LEI?
questions.explain: 'TNGB Credit exposure of Rs. 1.00 crore and above and advise them to obtain LEI.'

questions.q: At or above what proposal value is a TEV study from an outside agency required?
questions.explain: 'Credit proposals equal to and beyond Rs. 10.00 crore (fresh/addition/Expansions) should be accompanied by TEV study from an outside agency.'

questions.q: What is the maximum weight of gold coins accepted per customer?
questions.explain: 'Branch should ensure that the weight of the coin(s) does not exceed 50 grams per customer.'

questions.q: Above what credit facility value is external rating mandatory?
questions.explain: 'Credit facilities of value more than or equal to Rs. 5.00 crore, External Rating is mandatory.' Unrated eligible accounts are charged 0.75% extra.

questions.q: For how long are promoters involved in siphoning or diversion of funds debarred from institutional finance?
questions.explain: Such entrepreneurs/promoters 'should be debarred from institutional finance from the scheduled commercial banks for 5 years'.

questions.q: Up to what amount is no margin or security insisted on for agricultural loans, per RBI guidelines?
questions.explain: 'No margin and security shall be insisted for agricultural loans ... presently up to Rs. 2,00,000/-.'

questions.q: In SHG Panchasutra (M-S-L-R-B), what does 'L' stand for?
questions.explain: 'SHG Panchasutra: M – Meetings, S – Savings, L – Lending (Internal), R – Repayment, B – Bookkeeping.'

questions.q: What is the maximum credit limit for a Panchayat Level Federation (PLF) at the first linkage?
questions.explain: 'The Maximum credit limit for a PLF: 1st linkage Rs. 30.00 lakh and 2nd linkage onwards Rs. 50.00 lakh.'

questions.q: How many members can a Joint Liability Group (JLG) have?
questions.explain: 'JLG Financing – 4-10 Members.'

questions.q: For an Open Cash Credit, what margin applies on paid-for stocks and book debts?
questions.explain: Open Cash Credit: '25% on paid for stocks and Book Debts', with stocks and book debts under 180 days old as primary security.

questions.q: For home loans up to Rs. 30 lakh, what margin applies?
questions.explain: Home loan margins: up to Rs. 30 lakh – 10%; above Rs. 30 lakh up to Rs. 75 lakh – 20%; above Rs. 75 lakh – 25%; plot loans – 25%.

questions.q: For agricultural loan applications up to Rs. 25,000, what is the time limit for disposal?
questions.explain: Agriculture: up to Rs. 25,000 – within 15 days; beyond Rs. 25,000 up to Rs. 5 crore – within 4 weeks; above Rs. 5 crore – within 8 weeks.

questions.q: How is gold jewellery accepted as security valued?
options: At the average closing price of 22-carat gold over the preceding 30 days, as quoted by IBJA
questions.explain: Gold should be 'valued at the average of the closing price of 22 carat gold for the preceding 30 days as quoted by the India Bullion and Jewellers Association Ltd.'

questions.q: What is the maximum loan against own deposits (LOD) as a share of the deposit balance?
questions.explain: 'Loan / Overdraft up to a maximum of 90% of the balance outstanding in the deposits duly discharged by the depositor can be sanctioned.'

questions.q: What is the maximum period for an ad-hoc limit?
questions.explain: 'Adhoc limits can be sanctioned for a maximum period of THREE months', up to 30% of the original limit, at 1% above the regular rate.

questions.q: Which of these accounts is NOT eligible for takeover?
options: Standard accounts with two years of good conduct
Accounts with net profit in 2 of the last 3 years
questions.explain: Ineligible for takeover: accounts in Irregular/SMA/NPA, restructured accounts, accounts with an NPA group account, wilful defaulters and others.

questions.q: At or above what advance value must property security be valued by two independent valuers?
questions.explain: 'Properties accepted as security is to be valued by two independent valuers for advances of Rs. 100.00 lakh and above.'

questions.q: Up to what interest rate concession below the card rate can the General Manager Level Credit Committee (GMLCC) give?
questions.explain: Concession powers: MRPCLCC – 0.25%; RMLCC – 0.50%; GMLCC – 1.50%; CLCC – 2.50%; Board – more than 2.50%.

questions.q: Within what time must the Regional Manager carry out post-sanction inspection of stressed accounts sanctioned at Rs. 50 lakh and above?
questions.explain: RMs inspect such sanctions 'at least once in 6 months (in case of regular) and once in 3 months (in case of stressed accounts)'.

questions.q: Title deed and parent documents must be traced back how many years from the Sub-Registrar's office?
questions.explain: 'Certified copy of the title deeds and parent document tracing back to at least last 13 years from the title document should be obtained from the Sub Registrar's office.'

questions.q: Within how many days must creation, modification and satisfaction of security interest be reported to CERSAI?
questions.explain: 'The particulars of creation, modification and satisfaction of security interest ... are to be reported to the Central Registry (CERSAI) within 30 days.'

questions.q: What is the maximum aggregate weight of gold collateral for all loans to one borrower?
options: One kilogram, including at most 50 grams of gold coins
Two kilograms, with no coin limit
questions.explain: 'Aggregate weight of all loans against eligible gold collateral to a borrower shall not exceed one kilogram which includes maximum of 50 grams of gold coins.'

questions.q: Below what fineness is gold collateral NOT accepted?
questions.explain: 'Gold collateral below 18 carat fineness shall not be accepted as security.'

questions.q: For FY 2026-27, what is the TDS threshold for interest other than interest on securities (Sec 194A) for a senior citizen?
questions.explain: The TDS table gives the threshold under Sec 194A as Rs. 1,00,000 for a senior citizen and Rs. 50,000 for others.

questions.q: What is the TDS rate on interest (other than interest on securities) under Sec 194A if PAN is not available?
questions.explain: The table gives the rate as '10% (If PAN is not available 20%)'.

questions.q: Under Sec 194C (payment to contractors), what are the TDS thresholds?
options: A single payment of Rs. 20,000, or an aggregate of Rs. 50,000
A single payment of Rs. 50,000, or an aggregate of Rs. 5,00,000
A single payment of Rs. 30,000, or an aggregate of Rs. 1,00,000 in a financial year
questions.explain: For payment to contractors, the table gives 'Single payment: Rs. 30,000/- Aggregate in Financial Year: Rs. 1,00,000/-'.

questions.q: Under Sec 194C, what is the TDS rate when the deductee is an individual or HUF?
questions.explain: The rate is '1%: If deductee is an individual or HUF' and '2%: In any other case'.

questions.q: Under Sec 194I(b), what is the TDS rate on rent for land, building, furniture or fixtures?
questions.explain: The table gives '10%: If rent pertains to hiring of immovable property' (194I(b)), against 2% for plant and machinery (194I(a)).

questions.q: Above what threshold does TDS on rent apply under Sec 194I?
questions.explain: The table gives the rent threshold as 'Rs. 50000/Month'.

questions.q: Under Sec 194J, what is the TDS rate on fees for technical services?
questions.explain: The table gives '2%: If sum is payable towards fees for technical services'; professional fees and director fees attract 10%.

questions.q: Under Sec 194H (commission and brokerage), what are the threshold and the TDS rate?
questions.explain: The table lists Commission and Brokerage (194H) with a threshold of Rs. 20,000 and a TDS rate of 2%.

questions.q: Under Sec 194Q (payment for purchase of goods), what are the threshold and the TDS rate?
questions.explain: The table lists payment for purchase of goods (194Q) with a threshold of Rs. 50 lakhs and a rate of 0.10%.

questions.q: Under Sec 194N, above what amount of cash paid by a bank to a co-operative society does 2% TDS apply?
questions.explain: The table gives Rs. 3 crore at 2% for cash paid to a co-operative society, and Rs. 1 crore at 2% for cash paid to other deductees.

questions.q: Under Form 121, what is the threshold limit for an Indian resident individual or HUF below 60 years of age?
questions.explain: The Form 121 table lists a threshold of 50,000 for individuals and HUFs below 60 years, and 1,00,000 for senior citizens.

questions.q: Under Form 121, what is the exemption limit for a senior citizen (60 years and above) under the New regime?
questions.explain: For senior citizens, the exemption limit is 5,00,000 under the Old regime and 12,00,000 under the New regime.

questions.q: Under Form 121, what is the exemption limit for an individual below 60 years under the Old regime?
questions.explain: For individuals and HUFs below 60, the exemption limit is 2,50,000 under the Old regime and 4,00,000 under the New regime.

questions.q: What TDS rate applies if PAN is available but NOT linked with Aadhaar?
questions.explain: The table gives '10% if PAN available and Linked with Aadhaar' and '20% if PAN available and Not Linked with Aadhaar'.

questions.q: At what rate are branches advised to deduct TDS on NRO deposits?
questions.explain: 'Branches are advised to deduct TDS @ 31.20% (30%+4% Cess) for NRO deposits.'

questions.q: What surcharge on income-tax applies where total income is more than Rs. 1 crore and up to Rs. 2 crore?
questions.explain: The surcharge table: Nil up to Rs. 50 lakh; 10% above Rs. 50 lakh to Rs. 1 crore; 15% above Rs. 1 crore to Rs. 2 crore; 25% above Rs. 2 crore to Rs. 5 crore; 37% above Rs. 5 crore.

questions.q: When is Form 97 submitted?
options: When an individual without a PAN enters into certain transactions specified in Rule 159 of the Income-tax Rules, 1962
When a bank reports cash transactions to FIU-IND
When a person with only agricultural income opens an account
When a senior citizen claims non-deduction of TDS
questions.explain: 'Form 97 is ... submitted when an individual does not have a permanent account number and enters into certain transactions specified in Rule 159.' Form 61 is for people with only agricultural income.

questions.q: Under Rule 159, PAN (or Form 97) is mandatory for a time deposit with a bank exceeding:
options: Rs. 10 lakhs in a single deposit
Rs. 20,000, or an aggregate of more than Rs. 1 lakh
Rs. 50,000, or an aggregate of more than Rs. 5 lakhs in a financial year
Rs. 2 lakhs in a financial year
questions.explain: Rule 159 lists 'A time deposit with banks – Amount Exceeding Rs. 50000 or aggregate of more than Rs. 5 lakhs during financial year (PAN or Form 97 mandatory)'.

questions.q: Under the PMLA rules, banks must report all cash transactions above what value in a Cash Transaction Report (CTR)?
options: More than Rs. 10 lakh, or its equivalent in foreign currency
questions.explain: Banks must report 'All cash transactions of the value of more than rupees ten lakh or its equivalent in foreign currency', including integrally connected series within a month that together exceed Rs. 10 lakh.

questions.q: Under the STR rules, which transactions must be reported to FIU as suspicious?
options: Only for cash transactions above Rs. 10 lakh
Only for transactions with foreign customers
Only for completed transactions above Rs. 1 lakh
Suspicious transactions of any value, cash or non-cash, including attempted ones
questions.explain: A suspicious transaction is one 'including an attempted transaction, whether or not made in cash' that gives reasonable grounds of suspicion 'regardless of the value involved'.

questions.q: From what date has the MCLR system been effective?
questions.explain: 'MCLR system effective since 01.04.2016.' The Base Rate came in on 01.07.2010 and the external benchmark rate on 01.10.2019.

questions.q: What is the minimum number of MCLR tenors a bank must have?
questions.explain: 'Banks should have minimum 5 MCLR: (i) Overnight, (ii) 1-month, (iii) 3-month, (iv) 6-month & (v) 1-year MCLR.'

questions.q: Under the External Benchmark Based Lending Rate, for how long must the spread stay unchanged at minimum?
questions.explain: 'Spread: Bank can fix their own spread over the benchmark, which cannot be changed for minimum 3 years.'

questions.q: How often must interest be reset under EBLR, at a minimum?
questions.explain: 'Interest re-set: At least once in 3 months (can continue existing rate if linked benchmark has not changed).'

questions.q: Which section of the Banking Regulation Act empowers the RBI to apply Selective Credit Control?
questions.explain: 'SELECTIVE CREDIT CONTROL: Section 21 of Banking Regulations Act 1949.'

questions.q: Under the BCSBI code for MSEs, up to what loan amount is no collateral security required?
questions.explain: 'No collateral security for loans up to Rs. 10 lakh (in case of good track record, banks can waive it up to Rs. 25 lakh).'

questions.q: Under the BCSBI code for MSEs, within what time must securities be released after an account is closed?
questions.explain: 'Release of the securities held by the bank within 15 days of closure of accounts (if no other liabilities exist).'

questions.q: What is the maximum loan-to-value ratio for loans against gold jewellery, per the RBI directive?
questions.explain: 'Loan to Value Ratio for loan against gold jewellery: Maximum 90%.'

questions.q: In which year did the RBI create CRILC?
questions.explain: 'CRILC (Central Repository of Information on Large Credit) created by RBI in 2014.'

questions.q: What is the cut-off amount for reporting red-flagged accounts to the RBI?
questions.explain: 'Red Flagged Account ... Cut-off amount for reporting to RBI is Rs. 50 crore.'

questions.q: In fixing a KCC limit, what is added for post-harvest and consumption needs?
options: 25% of the limit, up to Rs. 50,000
10% of the limit, up to Rs. 25,000
20% of the limit, with no maximum
5% of the limit, up to Rs. 10,000
questions.explain: The KCC limit adds '10% post harvest consumption purpose (max of Rs. 25,000/-)' and '20% of limit for repairs and maintenance of farm mechanization'.

questions.q: For marginal farmers, what flexible KCC limit may be provided (Flexi KCC)?
questions.explain: 'A flexible limit of Rs. 10,000 to Rs. 50,000 may be provided (Flexi KCC).'

questions.q: A block where groundwater extraction is above 70% and up to 90% is classified as:
questions.explain: Stage of groundwater extraction: up to 70% – Safe; above 70% up to 90% – Semi-critical; above 90% up to 100% – Critical; above 100% – Over-exploited.

questions.q: What minimum family land holding makes a farmer eligible for a tractor loan?
options: 4 acres perennially irrigated or 8 acres unirrigated
questions.explain: Farmers with 'not less than 4 acres of perennially irrigated land or 8 acres of unirrigated area (dry land) are eligible for purchase of tractors'.

questions.q: For financing a pre-used tractor, what is the maximum age of the tractor and the maximum loan?
options: Not more than seven years; Rs. 1.50 lakh
Not more than ten years; Rs. 1 lakh
Not more than three years; Rs. 2 lakh
Not more than five years; Rs. 3 lakh
questions.explain: 'Age of tractor not more than seven years. Maximum loan amount: Rs. 1.50 lakh.'

questions.q: Under the Nayak Committee turnover method, what working capital limit can be given?
options: 20% of projected turnover (25% requirement minus a 5% borrower contribution)
25% of projected turnover, fully by the bank
questions.explain: 'TURNOVER METHOD – NAYAK COMMITTEE: 20% of projected TO/sales', from a working capital requirement of 25% of sales, of which the borrower contributes 5%.

questions.q: Who chaired the RBI study group (1974) that recommended the Maximum Permissible Bank Finance (MPBF) methods?
questions.explain: 'A Study Group under the chairmanship of Mr. Prakash Tandon, the then Chairman and Managing Director of Punjab National Bank was constituted by the Reserve Bank of India in July 1974.'

questions.q: Above what term loan amount must a sensitivity analysis be carried out?
questions.explain: 'Term loans of above Rs. 1 crore, sensitivity analysis to be done', e.g. 5% rise in expenses, 5% fall in revenue, 10% rise in capex, 10% fall in sale price.

questions.q: In the internal risk rating scale, which score range corresponds to grade 'A'?
questions.explain: Internal ratings: AAA 9.5+; AA+ 8.5–9.5; AA 7.5–8.5; A 6.5–7.5; BBB 5.5–6.5; BB 4.5–5.5; and so on.

questions.q: What is the maximum loan ceiling for a four-wheeler vehicle loan?
questions.explain: 'Maximum loan ceiling: a. Two Wheelers – Rs. 5.00 lakh; b. Four Wheelers – Rs. 200.00 lakh (including used car).'

questions.q: On whose recommendations were prudential accounting norms (IRACP) introduced in banks in 1993?
options: The Narasimham Committee on Financial Sector Reforms (1991)
questions.explain: 'On recommendations of Narasimhan Committee on Financial Sector Reforms (1991) Prudential Accounting Norms have been implemented in Banks (1993).'

questions.q: An account whose principal or interest is overdue for 31 to 60 days is classified as:
questions.explain: SMA-0 – overdue up to 30 days; SMA-1 – 31 to 60 days; SMA-2 – 61 to 90 days.

questions.q: How is an NPA classified after 2 years and up to 4 years from the NPA date?
questions.explain: Substandard – up to 1 year; Doubtful 1 – 1 to 2 years; Doubtful 2 – 2 to 4 years; Doubtful 3 – after 4 years from the NPA date.

questions.q: What provision is required on the secured portion of a Doubtful 1 asset?
questions.explain: Provision on the secured portion: Substandard 10%; Doubtful 1 – 20%; Doubtful 2 – 30%; Doubtful 3 and Loss – 100%. The unsecured portion of doubtful assets needs 100%.

questions.q: What general provision is required on standard advances to Commercial Real Estate?
questions.explain: Standard asset provisions: Agriculture and SMEs – 0.25%; Commercial Real Estate – 1%; Residential Real Estate – 0.75%; All other loans – 0.40%.

questions.q: A short-duration crop loan becomes NPA when principal or interest is overdue for:
questions.explain: Short duration crops are NPA 'if instalment of principal or interest thereon remains overdue for the period of two crop season'. Long duration crops: one crop season.

questions.q: When is a CC/OD account treated as NPA for non-review or non-renewal of its limit?
options: Never; non-review does not cause NPA
When the limit has not been reviewed or renewed for more than 180 days
questions.explain: CC & OD accounts become NPA on 'Non-review / non-renewal of limit for more than 180 days', among other triggers.

questions.q: When is an asset directly classified as a Loss asset because security value has eroded?
options: When it is less than 50% of the assessed value
When the realisable value of security is less than 10% of the outstanding
When it is less than 75% of the outstanding
questions.explain: Below 50% of the assessed value makes the asset Doubtful, and 'if it is less than 10% of the outstanding as Loss asset'.

questions.q: Within what time must red-flagged accounts be reported to the RBI's Central Fraud Monitoring Cell?
questions.explain: 'Reporting to be made to the Central Fraud Monitoring Cell of RBI, within 1 month.'

questions.q: What minimum upfront amount must be collected from the borrower with an OTS proposal?
questions.explain: 'Obtention of a minimum upfront amount of 10% from the borrower is mandatory. The upfront amount may be kept in a Sundry Deposit.'

questions.q: Within what time must the OTS amount be paid in one lump sum after the sanction is communicated?
questions.explain: 'OTS amount should be recovered in one lump sum within 90 days from the date of communication of OTS sanction. Failing which the Sanction becomes void.'

questions.q: In what order are recoveries in an NPA account appropriated?
options: Principal (book balance), then legal expenses (MLE), then other charges (MOX), then unpaid interest (MOI)
Legal expenses first, then interest, then principal
questions.explain: 'Any Recovery should be first appropriated to Book Balance (Principal) and then to Unpaid Legal Expenses (MLE), then to other charges (MOX) and thereafter to Unpaid Interest (MOI).'

questions.q: In NPV calculations for OTS, what cost of realisation is assumed?
questions.explain: 'Cost of realisation to be determined as 10% of RV of the security irrespective of amount.'

questions.q: Above what outstanding amount (BB + MOI) is a borrower who has wilfully defaulted treated as a wilful defaulter?
questions.explain: 'A borrower or a guarantor who has committed wilful default and the outstanding amount (BB+MOI) is Rs. 25 lakh and above shall be construed as wilful defaulter.'

questions.q: Within how many days of the show-cause notice must the borrower respond to the Identification Committee?
questions.explain: The Identification Committee issues a show-cause notice and calls for submissions 'within 21 days of issuance of show cause notice'.

questions.q: For how long after removal from the List of Wilful Defaulters is credit for new ventures barred?
questions.explain: 'No credit facility shall be granted ... for floating of new ventures to a wilful defaulter ... for a period of 5 years after the name of wilful defaulter has been removed from the LWD.'

questions.q: On which day each month are Lok Adalats held?
questions.explain: Courts organise 'Lok Adalats within their area of jurisdiction on 2nd Saturday of every month', for claims up to Rs. 20 lakh.

questions.q: The DRT Act applies to debts due to banks above what amount?
questions.explain: 'The Act is applicable for the debt due (Both secured and Unsecured) ... when the debt is above 20.00 Lakh Rupees.'

questions.q: Under Section 13(2) of SARFAESI, how much time does the demand notice give the borrower to pay?
questions.explain: 'Under Sec. 13(2) of the Act, Demand notice of 60 days to discharge the debt in full to be issued.'

questions.q: For SARFAESI action, the outstanding amount (book balance + MOI) must be more than:
questions.explain: SARFAESI eligibility: account must be NPA, outstanding 'should be more than Rs. 1.00 lakh', dues above 20% of principal and interest, and the asset not agricultural land.
